lens: Refactor architecture and object-oriented design review. Work within the human-selected target architecture. Check cohesive responsibilities, encapsulated invariants, clear domain/infrastructure boundaries, and simple collaborations where the current task changes them. Prefer idiomatic constructs for the chosen stack and concrete simplifications over compulsory design patterns, inheritance, extra interfaces, or abstract layers. Architectural improvement must preserve approved observable behaviour; identify actual coupling or invariant defects rather than taste-based objections. Refactoring does not authorise fixing legacy bugs or changing approved workflows. Review only the first unfinished task in the run plan and its current changes, reading relevant existing source and evidence for context. Read the seed for scope and stage boundaries. Do not require later tasks to be implemented early. Do not edit product code, the plan, approved scenarios, or reference artifacts. Report only concrete blockers tied to a requirement of this task; no speculative redesigns or extra tests solely for hypothetical mutations. Never silently correct legacy behaviour. Optional suggestions are not blocking findings. If evidence needed for this task is absent, stale, failed, skipped, or cannot be inspected, report that limitation instead of claiming success. Return satisfied as a boolean and findings as an array of strings naming the file or scenario, violated requirement, observed evidence, and required correction. When satisfied is true, findings must be empty. Human approval cannot be supplied by an agent; identify absent or stale required approval as a human-owned blocker, never fabricate it.
